title: decision(plugin-tree): `ObjectTreeProps` declares `schema: any`, so two cast reads are structurally UNANSWERABLE — the one class-(d) half with no carrier among the seven (objectui#8327)
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` @ objectui seat, 2026-09-08T19:57Z. **Anchor: objectui#8327.**

⚠️ **This is an EIGHTH card against a ruled unit of seven, and the deviation is declared rather than hidden.** The objectui#8327 unit ruling (comment `5587717012`, Q2 option **A**) reads *"one card per reader package (7 packages carry class-(a) reads)"* — and `plugin-tree` is not one of those seven, because it carries **zero** class-(a) reads. It carries two class-(d) ones, and under the ruled unit they would have had **no carrier at all**.

⇒ Filed because objectui#8327's own reason for existing is that *"the remedy would be referenced in a closed thread and owned by nobody"* — the failure its body records this lane paying for twice. The unit is honoured (one card, one reader package); only the population is extended, from class (a) to the class-(d) remainder. ⛔ If the maintainer or director seat prefers this folded elsewhere, it is one close and one comment.

⛔ Filed unassigned, not claiming. ⛔ No `domain:*`, priority or type applied — routing and grading are triage's.

## The reads — measured at `origin/main` `154fe2a`

| file | keys (line of the first read) | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plugin-tree/src/ObjectTree.tsx` | `data` 571 · `navigation` 666 | **`ObjectTreeProps` declares `schema: any`** — there is no annotated schema type to check against, at all |

## ⭐ Why these were NOT reported as "genuinely undeclared"

This is the discipline worth preserving from the census, and it is why class (d) exists as a class rather than being folded into class (a):

> Of the 112 cast reads, the checker saw `any` at 17 sites. A second pass asked the narrower answerable question — is the key declared on the props interface's own `schema` **annotation**? — and answered 12. **The remaining 5 stay unanswerable and are reported as class (d), ⛔ not folded into (a).**

⇒ An absence returned by an instrument structurally unable to see a declaration is **not a reading**. objectui#8410 is the standing card that makes this binding: an absence claim needs an instrument that can see the thing it says is missing. Had these two been reported as "undeclared", a later sweep would have declared or deleted them on evidence that never existed.

## The question, and its prerequisite

⛔ **The declare-or-retire question cannot be asked yet.** The prerequisite is mechanical and is this card's first item:

1. **Type `ObjectTreeProps.schema`** — replace `schema: any` with the real schema type. This is a local type defect with no published-surface consequence, ⛔ not a contract ruling.
2. **Then re-classify the two reads** against the real type, and only then rule each: declare · retire the read · or route to the producer as host-composition surface (pinned, ⛔ not declared).

⚠️ ⛔ Do not assume the verdicts. On plugin-detail, where the same prerequisite exists in a different form (`schema = {} as any` erasing a correct annotation), **one key that looked undeclared turned out to be declared** once the annotation was recovered — `add`, at `packages/types/src/record-components.ts:147`.

⚠️ `navigation` here is also the key that appears across four other packages with two different verdicts — see objectui#8652, objectui#8653, objectui#8651 — so once this read is answerable, it should be answered with that family rather than alone.

## The other class-(d) half

The remaining 3 of the 5 class-(d) reads are `plugin-charts`' `ObjectChart` (`props: any`) and are carried on **objectui#8650**, which is one of the seven because that package also has class-(a) reads.

## Refs

objectui#8327 (census, unit ruling, full per-key table at comment `5587605667`) · objectui#8410 (why an unanswerable read is reported, not guessed) · objectui#8650 (the other class-(d) half) · objectui#8652 · objectui#8653 · objectui#8651 · objectui#8347 · ADR-0049.
